Hi Emma —

Thanks for the call earlier. Picking up on Sunridge’s redlines to the MSA / order form: the primary live issue from your side seems to be (1) control of defense for third-party IP claims tied to model outputs, and (2) the scope of indemnity when customer-provided training data was used to fine-tune a model.

Quick proposal to move forward and unblock procurement:
- Redwood is willing to accept defense control for third-party claims that arise solely from Sunridge’s materials (customer-supplied training data or prompts) where there is a clear prima facie link.
- For claims that allege infringement or misappropriation based on model-generated output where causation is ambiguous, Redwood requests the ability to (a) lead the defense or (b) reimburse customer for reasonable defense costs if Redwood chooses not to defend.
- Notification windows: 10 business days to notify Redwood; cooperation required; evidence custody to be shared via a secure evidence matrix (see attached template).
- Insurance offset: proceed as proposed by Sunridge but limit to amounts actually recovered from applicable insurance; Redwood will not pass through unrelated deductibles.

If that sounds close, can you confirm which points are non-starters for Sunridge so I can loop in Kimberly (legal) and Ben (sales) with specifics? I’ve attached our recommended redline baseline and an evidence matrix we use for triage.

Thanks —

Thanks for the context. Below is a compact, negotiable drafting approach we can propose to Sunridge — aim is to balance operational control and exposure: 

Suggested clause (draft language to insert into Section X - Indemnification):

"Third-party IP claims arising solely from Customer-Supplied Materials. If a third party asserts a claim that the Customer-Supplied Materials (as defined herein) infringe such third party's intellectual property rights, Customer shall have the right to assume and control the defense of such claim, provided Customer notifies Redwood within ten (10) business days of receipt of the claim and provides all reasonably requested evidence. Redwood shall reasonably cooperate with Customer's defense. Redwood may, at its option, assume control of the defense upon notice to Customer, in which case Redwood shall indemnify Customer for damages finally awarded against Customer and reasonable, documented defense costs."

"Model-Output Claims. For claims alleging that Model-Generated Output infringes a third party’s rights, Redwood shall have the initial right to assume and control the defense. If Redwood declines to defend such a claim in good faith within fifteen (15) business days after notice, Redwood shall (i) reimburse Customer for reasonable, documented defense costs incurred before Redwood assumed defense, and (ii) not assert its declination for the purpose of compelling Customer to settle except where settlement is necessary to avoid disproportionate exposure and Redwood consents. The Parties agree to a good-faith escalation process (technical review + joint counsel call) prior to any settlement."

"Insurance and Offset. Any indemnity payment shall be reduced by amounts actually recovered from applicable insurance covering the claim; however, Redwood shall first tender the claim to its insurers and use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain coverage prior to requiring Customer to claim under Customer's insurance for claims Redwood has accepted to defend."

Operational notes: include an evidence matrix (attached) and an agreed privileged channel for exchanging technical artifacts (SFTP or pre-authorized secure share). Recommend we accept the above as a counterproposal; if Sunridge insists on unconditional defense-control for model-output claims, we should request either a monetary cap or a premium credit.

Ben — commercial fallback: we can offer a 6-month fee credit (up to $50k) as partial concession in exchange for the expanded defense-control carveout, or alternatively agree to a higher per-unit price for fine-tuning/hosted private deployments. Which would you prefer to propose?
